_why: Passage summaries decided by hand, keyed by passage id. 'held': hidden although every check passes, with the reason (a misattributed quotation the gate cannot see). 'approved': shown although flagged, only while the text is the one John read (sha256 of it). Nothing here is shown as John's words (rule 2): approval decides visibility, never text. Held on 15 Oct 2026 while reading the newly shown summaries; John approves or rejects through the review queue.

GEN.46.16-46.18.fix:
Relationship to Jacob and Zilpah	Count
Sons: Gad and Asher	2
Grandchildren: Gad’s seven sons and Asher’s five children, including Serah	12
Great-grandchildren: Heber and Malchiel, sons of Beriah	2
Total	16


JPS uses “descendants of Zilpah,” which accurately covers everyone listed. www.sefaria.org
Required fix: Replace “children and grandchildren” with “descendants.” Zilpah’s servant status is supported by Genesis 29:24. www.chabad.org
“Those” is clear alongside the family list; for a standalone

EXO.22.16-22.31.fix:
The excerpt joins two unrelated laws without explaining the transition.
- “Throw it” has no clear referent. It means meat from an animal torn by beasts, which Israelites were forbidden to eat. It has no connection to the preceding marriage law. This missing context is the biggest problem. The Sefaria Library
- “Tricks” is too specific. Hebrew יְפַתֶּה (yefatteh) is rendered “seduces” by JPS; Rashi explains persuasion or enticement. Deception is not explicitly required by the wording. The Sefaria

HEB.11.20-11.22.fix:
The meaning is sound, but Joseph’s example is too vague.
- “Because he trusted God” reasonably expresses πίστει (pistei), “by faith,” which introduces each example.
- Isaac and Jacob’s blessings are accurately described. Joseph’s two sons were Ephraim and Manasseh; “his son” correctly clarifies Joseph’s relationship to Jacob. Bible Gateway
- “Joseph’s prophecy and command” needs explaining. He anticipated the Israelites’ departure from Egypt and instructed them to carry his bones with them. Gene

NUM.1.5-1.16.fix: 'They' should be the named tribal leaders, appointed to help Moses and Aaron with the census.

NUM.4.1-4.20.fix: Explain the division: Aaron and his sons cover the holy things; the Kohathites carry them without touching. Sanctuary-entry wording obscures it.

DEU.18.9-18.14.fix: Name the forbidden practices: divination, sorcery, consulting the dead, child sacrifice. 'Disgusting things' and 'that' leave it unexplained.

DEU.20.1-20.20.fix: Twenty verses of war laws: include exemptions, approaching cities, protecting fruit trees.

DEU.25.5-25.12.fix: Include the brother's marriage duty and the public refusal; 'same property' too specific; range also holds a separate law (vv.11–12).

JOS.13.29-13.33.fix: Sentence is about Levi, not Manasseh. Summarise eastern Manasseh's territory, then Levi's inheritance separately.

JDG.2.6-2.9.fix: Naming Joshua's father isn't a summary of his death: 110 years, burial, Israel served the LORD in his generation.

1KI.6.11-6.13.fix: Restore the condition of obedience; the promise is to dwell among Israel, 'in it' narrows it.

2CH.32.32-33.9.fix: Include Hezekiah's death and burial; range runs through Manasseh's idolatry (33:9): fix the boundary or broaden.

EZR.2.1-2.67.fix: A partial list, not a summary: the returning families and temple staff, total 42,360; not every designation is a town.

EZR.6.1-6.12.fix: Say what the archive search found and what Darius ordered: allow, fund and supply the rebuilding. 'I make this decree' has no substance.

EZR.8.21-8.23.fix: Hebrew 'aph' is anger here, not nose. Central action: fasting and seeking protection, God answered.

NEH.5.14-5.19.fix: Nehemiah declined the governor's allowance and fed others at his own cost; 'do this' should be his prayer to be remembered.

NEH.10.1-10.27.fix: Not only priests: Nehemiah, Levites and leaders sealed the covenant. Summarise the groups, not one group's names.

ECC.2.18-2.26.fix: Omits the conclusion: enjoying food, drink and work is God's gift.

ISA.32.9-32.20.fix: Punctuation; restore the turn: complacency, devastation, then renewal when the Spirit is poured out.

ISA.53.1-53.8.fix: 'Who has believed our report?' is rhetorical. Keep the contrast between the speakers' misjudgment and the servant suffering for others. 'No descendants' is interpretive; readings of servant and speakers differ.

JER.4.1-4.4.fix: Shorten the long conditional; include inward repentance (heart imagery) and the judgment warning (vv.3–4).

JER.11.18-11.23.fix: Substitutes Jeremiah's commissioning for the passage: God reveals the plot against Jeremiah; judgment on the men of Anathoth.

JER.13.12-13.14.fix: Hebrew makes God the subject of dashing them together, parents and children; 'Parents will bash their children' changes the actor.

JER.16.14-16.21.fix: State the restoration promise and its comparison with the exodus; include the judgment and the nations knowing God.

JER.22.24-22.30.fix: Add the royal consequence: none of Coniah's offspring will prosper on David's throne.

JER.25.1-25.14.fix: Include seventy years serving Babylon, then judgment on Babylon; the selection stops before the prophecy's substance.

JER.29.1-29.23.fix: Says who the letter is to, not its message: settle in Babylon, seek the city's welfare, reject false promises, return after seventy years.

DAN.5.1-5.4.fix: Explain 'those cups': the sacred vessels from the Jerusalem temple, used while praising idols.

ZEC.7.1-7.14.fix: Two sentences repeat the question's background; include God's answer: justice, mercy, care for the vulnerable, past disobedience.

MAT.26.17-26.19.fix: Introduce the man whose house is used; keep to the preparations, the meal starts after the passage.

LUK.20.45-20.47.fix: Name the scribes and Jesus as speaker; their exploiting widows and greater condemnation, not only display.

LUK.22.63-22.65.fix: Remove 'took turns' (unsupported); include the taunt 'who struck you?'. Heading 'The Guards Mock Jesus'.

EPH.2.19-2.22.fix: Add the apostles-and-prophets foundation, Christ the cornerstone, a dwelling for God by the Spirit.

PHP.2.1-2.4.fix: Add the practice: humility, no selfish ambition, others' interests.

COL.3.22-3.25.fix: The audience is slaves under earthly masters; include work as for Christ, the inheritance, impartial judgment.
